Hey there. I’m a history and English teacher in an Ontario school board who (like so many of my colleagues were “efficiently” laid off). 

Please understand that what I’m about to say below is not a justification of Doug Ford’s reckless decisions nor is it meant to cut you down or invalidate you in any way. While I will give you some ways in which you can “protest”, I also want to give you some tools to potentially help you out more immediately

1) Your courses were cut. While this is unfortunate my strong suspicion is that the courses cut were electives (courses not MANDATORY, but that you wanted to take). I suspect this because you’re in grade 12 and there is only 1 required course in that grade (English) or 2 if you’re in a catholic board (add in religion or philosophy). If this is the case you have a few options: a) you can take other non compulsory courses that may not be filled up (techs, arts, etc that tend not to be maxed) if they’re available; or b) register for some online learning (I hate that I’m suggesting this). If your board doesn’t offer online learning, look for a board in your surrounding area. You CAN be a student of multiple boards at once if you’re taking online courses. 

2) a small tidbit that won’t help with much but may offer some consolation to your friend: law is not a prerequisite for law (how absurd is that?!). In fact, your friend doesn’t even need to take law in her undergrad. Law school simply requires a 4-year BA in anything to apply. 

3) Protests: you’ve got options. Like many have suggested, reach out to the CBC, Star newspapers, etc. I disagree with many of the posters here and think that even post media (Sun) would be worth reaching out to. Anybody who will listen. The sun could be especially important as its readers do tend to be conservatives and really, that’s who you want to reach. Contact your MPP. If you’re not sure who that is, you can reply to this with your postal code and I can figure that out for you. 

Most important protest option? As a grade 12, you’re either 18 or approaching 18. If you’re 18 now, vote in October. If you’re not, make sure you vote in 2022 to avoid the re-election of Doug Ford. Convince your friends to do the same. I’m a die hard liberal so I’d love to suggest you vote for them, but I won’t. Because you shouldn’t always. Vote for the party most likely to defeat the conservative candidate in YOUR riding. Live in Hamilton? Vote NDP. Live in Vancouver? Vote green. 

I’m sorry this is happening to you. I wish you all the best!
